newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan June trade surplus seen up 37%-research body.
newsitem.headline: Japan June trade surplus seen up 37%-research body.

text.p: Japan's customs-cleared trade surplus is seen rising 37.4 percent to 1.01 trillion yen in June, compared with the year-earlier period, the Daiwa Bank Research Institute said in a report on Friday.
The institute said exports are likely to rise 18.6 percent in June from a year earlier to 4.35 trillion yen, while imports are seen increasing by 13.9 percent to 3.34 trillion yen.
The growth in the trade surplus in June is expected to be smaller than that of preceding months -- a 158 percent rise in April and a 222 percent surge in May.

The expected slowdown in the growth of the surplus is mainly due to increases in imports both in value and volume terms, caused partly by a stronger yen against the dollar during June, it said. Import volumes are seen up 10.3 percent in June.
